snippet: The case was identified following the clinical deterioration and death of an adult male patient from the DRC who was admitted to a private hospital in Kampala, Uganda, in May 2026. Demographic information, including patient sex and travel history from the DRC, was extracted from a standardized national VHF case investigation form and the electronic case admission record. Given the clinical course, an incomplete epidemiological history and regional concern for VHF, a posthumous EDTA whole-blood [...] no blood work was performed before he left, and then self-referred to a private hospital in Kampala. On admission on 11 May 2026, the patient presented with severe vomiting, frequent diarrhea, intermittent epigastric pain, generalized weakness and hiccups; vomiting and diarrhea had reportedly persisted for more than 2 weeks, although the exact symptom onset date was not ascertained. title: EBOLA BUNDIBUGYO VIRUS DISEASE OUTBREAK Democratic Republic of the Congo | Uganda Weekly External Situation Report 11, Data as of 26 July 2026 | WHO | Regional Office for Africa
snippet:
The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continued to intensify during the reporting period, with sustained transmission, increasing mortality, and ongoing geographic expansion within the country. The cumulative number of reported cases has exceeded the two previously documented Bundibugyo virus disease outbreaks, making this the largest outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus to date. Although no new cases have been reported outside the Democratic [...] the Democratic Republic of the Congo, persistent transmission in areas connected by major national and cross-border mobility corridors continues to sustain a high risk of regional spread. These epidemiological trends underscore the need for strengthened surveillance, cross-border collaboration, and preparedness to rapidly detect and contain any international spread.
